answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewal and negotiation cannot deliver the mandated 18% cut, and deferral is impossible since the contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. Adding a second source protects supply but does not cut cost this cycle. That leaves switching to the low-cost vendor as the only lever capable of hitting the target. Memory c2 reports that vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — it is the load-bearing claim for this move, so I verify it before committing. Given the line runs at 94% with zero buffer, I would execute the switch as a guarded, phased cutover (initial allocation, hold a bridge arrangement with the incumbent if possible) rather than a full immediate flip, and treat memory c4's benchmark data as supporting evidence that market rates justify the cost target. Downstream delivery risk is real and flagged: the cutover plan must include inventory cover for the transition window.
